correctness.rationale: Alspach's theorem gives, for each base arc, a containing base cycle of every length \(3\le t\le c\). For any target \(\ell\), the integer intervals \([3k,ck]\), \(1\le k\le\alpha\), cover all lengths 3 through \(c\alpha\) when \(c\ge5\). Writing \(\ell=t_1+\cdots+t_k\) with each \(t_j\in[3,c]\), choose k base cycles containing the prescribed arc and lift them on distinct layer indices. Concatenating each cycle's terminal-to-u arc into the next layer gives a simple directed cycle of length \(\ell\); distinct layers prevent repeated lifted vertices. The c=3 exclusion is genuine.
correctness.risk: The argument uses equal part sizes and a blow-up orientation inherited from one regular base tournament; it does not extend automatically to arbitrary regular multipartite tournaments.

evidence: Xia is broader in allowing arbitrary regular multipartite orientations, but only for c>=93 and lengths >=4.
Pan--Zhang is broader in multipartite orientation but tracks partite-set count rather than cycle length.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Those broader ambient classes do not dominate the all-c>=5, all-length 3..c alpha statement on the blow-up subclass.

evidence: Alspach supplies the base cycles but does not itself show how to combine repeated lifted layers into arbitrary larger lengths.
The submitted interval decomposition \([3k,ck]\) and layerwise splicing provide that missing implication.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The lift is short but requires a new constructive argument; neither a part-count cycle theorem nor the c>=93 general theorem yields the small-c conclusion.

evidence: Alspach: every arc of a regular tournament lies on every cycle length 3 through the order.
Pan--Zhang: every arc lies on a cycle meeting exactly k partite sets for k=4,...,n.
Xia: general regular equal-part c-partite tournaments are 4-arc-pancyclic for c>=93.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: No equivalent theorem for lexicographic/equal independent-set blow-ups of an arbitrary regular tournament was located.
searches: Resultary: regular tournament equal blow-up arc pancyclic multipartite tournament

evidence: No exact table or database of cycle lengths for equal blow-ups was found.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: The theorem is proved uniformly by splicing and is not a finite census.

originality.rationale: Alspach proves arc-pancyclicity only in a regular tournament, while Pan--Zhang's regular multipartite result controls the number of partite sets met, not every vertex length. Xia's 2026 theorem gives all lengths from 4 upward only for arbitrary regular equal-part multipartite tournaments with at least 93 parts. The submitted theorem is an exact full-length result, including triangles, for the natural equal-blow-up subclass for every regular base order \(c\ge5\). No checked composition theorem states this lift.
residual_risks: An older digraph-composition theorem under lexicographic-product terminology may encode the same splicing result; targeted searches did not surface one.

source_inspections.evidence: It guarantees cycles using exactly k partite sets for k=4,...,n, not a cycle of every vertex length.

source_inspections.evidence: It proves every arc lies on all cycle lengths 4..c alpha for c>=93; the audited result covers the structured blow-ups for every regular c>=5 and adds length 3.
source_inspections.title: 4-Arc-Pancyclicity of Regular Multipartite Tournaments
source_inspections.trigger: Current strongest general equal-part regular multipartite result.

value.rationale: This gives complete arc-pancyclicity on a natural infinite subclass of regular multipartite tournaments for every admissible base order \(c\ge5\), far below the current general c>=93 range. It also includes triangles and supplies an explicit cycle construction, so it is a motivated structural special-class theorem rather than a small parameter improvement.
value.risk: The splicing construction is elementary once Alspach's theorem is known, and the result does not classify unequal blow-ups.

final_claim: If \(T\) is a regular tournament on \(c\ge5\) vertices and every vertex is blown up to an independent set of equal size \(\alpha\), then every arc of the blow-up lies on a directed cycle of every length \(3,4,\ldots,c\alpha\).
limitations: The theorem does not cover unequal blow-ups or arbitrary regular multipartite tournaments.
The c=3 equal blow-up can miss intermediate lengths for alpha>=2.
